Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed graph implemented with an adjacency list, the cost of processing vertex v equals its out-degree, so the worst-case single operation and the amortized cost depend on how edges are distributed among vertices.

* (a) The worst possible single operation has a cost of **|E|**, which occurs when all edges in the graph are outgoing from a single vertex v, making the out-degree of v equal to the total number of edges.
* (b) The average amortized cost per operation, computed via aggregate analysis, is **|E| / |V|**, since the total cost over the entire sequence of |V| operations is exactly the sum of all out-degrees, which equals |E|, and dividing by |V| gives the amortized cost per operation.
